name: Balanced 4-4-2

slots.why: Distributes directly to the strikers or full-backs; no sweeping needed in a flat block.
Support full-back gives width behind the winger and covers when the winger goes forward.
Central defender in a flat pair. Cover is the alternate.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but at most one of the pair can be Cover.
Winger (Support) provides width and crosses for the two strikers.
Defensive central midfielder screens the defence and does the simple work.
Supporting central midfielder links the wingers and strikers with the defensive midfielder.
Winger (Support) on the right, giving the same width and crossing.
Deep-lying forward (or Complete Forward) holds the ball and links with the other striker.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence; Poacher is the alternate for a striker who finishes better than he runs.

description: A simple two-banks-of-four structure with natural width and two complementary forwards.
whyGood: It is easy to recruit for, tactically clear and gives a useful baseline against more specialised systems.
whyThisShape: Two flat banks of four with two strikers, the most familiar shape in the game. It is easy to understand, gives every player a clear job, and puts two strikers against two centre-backs. It is thin in central midfield against a three.
whenToUse: As a solid default, or when you have two good strikers and two decent wingers. It is also the shape most lower-league squads can fill without a specialist.
whenNotToUse: Against a team with three central midfielders who will pass through the middle, since your two are outnumbered.

instructionRationale.Fairly Wide: Wingers and full-backs stretch the opponent so the two strikers have space.
instructionRationale.Slightly More Direct Passing: Gets the ball to the strikers quicker than short passing does, which suits a pair of forwards.
instructionRationale.Counter: Breaks quickly when the ball is won, using the pace of the wingers and second striker.
instructionRationale.Regroup: Falls back into the two banks of four after losing the ball.
instructionRationale.Standard Line of Engagement: A balanced press: engages when the ball reaches the midfield banks.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: A balanced line keeps the block compact.
